records.name: 5 Shorts Project
records.summary: A Philadelphia film group that helps local residents make their own short films, with no filmmaking background needed. It also runs teen film programs and a yearly teen film festival.
records.what_you_do: Work through the free filmmaking tutorials on the Learn Filmmaking page, join a teen summer session that makes a film, or attend the Teen Film Fest.

schedule.text: The free tutorials have no set dates. Teen sessions run twice a week for 5 hours a day, mostly in summer. The 2026 Teen Film Fest was on July 25.

cost.text: The tutorials and teen sessions are free. Teen sessions include a stipend, meals, and transportation costs. An optional Community Membership is $15 a month, with sliding-scale fees and scholarships.

access.notes: The About page links to an accessibility page, but the content we read lists no features.

first_step.how: Start with one free Learn Filmmaking tutorial, then email hello@5shorts.org to ask about the next teen session and its application.
first_step.basis: The tutorials list no prerequisites, the homepage says no experience is needed, and the teen program explains how to apply by email.
first_step.what_to_expect: The tutorials each cover one filmmaking skill, such as writing a script, planning shots, sound, lighting, or editing, and they cost nothing. Teen sessions run about 5 hours at a time, twice a week in summer, with a stipend and meals. The site does not describe a first-day routine, so ask the team what to expect.
first_visit_tips: Email hello@5shorts.org for the application and the next session dates
Ask where Germantown sessions meet and how to get there
Look at the Teen Film Fest page to see what the group's films look like

records.notes: The teen program pages list ages 12 to 18 across two sessions (Germantown Amplified and Bout Mine I Matter). A separate invitation-only internship (What's For Dinner) is not open to the public, so it is not listed as a way in. Membership fee is optional. The Eventbrite ticket page was not read.

records.name: A Forbidden Fruit
records.summary: A creative wellness group that puts on free events, a community garden project called the Giving Garden, and a yearly one-day festival of art, food, and movement.
records.what_you_do: Go to a free event, help with Giving Garden projects as a volunteer, or sign up for the mailing list to hear about the next program. The 2026 festival has already happened.

schedule.text: The 2026 Root 2 Fruit festival ran Sept 12 from noon to 6 pm. As of Oct 8, 2026, no upcoming events are listed.

cost.text: The Root 2 Fruit festival was free. Costs for other events are not stated.

access.notes: The festival page says the group aims to make events accessible but lists no specific accommodations.

first_step.how: Sign up for the Harvest Hub mailing list on the site to hear about the next event, then check the programs page.
first_step.basis: Events are public and the site offers a mailing list and a volunteer form, but no event is listed right now and the site does not say how beginners are welcomed.
first_step.what_to_expect: The festival was a free, one-day event with workshops, yoga, food, and dance, running from noon to 6 pm. Smaller Giving Garden events and other programs are announced by newsletter and social media, and their format changes from event to event. No event is listed as of Oct 8, 2026.
first_visit_tips: Sign up for the mailing list so you hear about the next event
The site lists no public email or phone, so use the contact form on the Contact page
Look at the Past Events page to see what a typical event was like

records.notes: The Giving Garden page lists three events with no dates or venues. Volunteer and sponsor sign-ups are Google Form links on the site; they were not submitted. The site says the 2025 recap has no events, so the group's public activity is mostly the annual festival and smaller events.

records.name: ACCT Philly
records.summary: The city's open intake animal shelter on Hunting Park Avenue. Volunteers walk dogs, help at adoption events, and care for cats at adoption centers, and people can foster animals until they are adopted.
records.what_you_do: Walk dogs or care for cats at the shelter, help at adoption events, staff the in-store adoption centers, bring a group for a laundry or food pantry project, or foster an animal.

schedule.text: The shelter lobby is open 7 days a week from 10 am to 6 pm. Volunteers finish an online orientation on their own time, and shelter volunteers commit at least 3 hours a month. Adoption events run Oct 9 to 16 and Oct 23 to 24, 2026.

cost.text: Volunteering and fostering are unpaid. A $10 cat adoption special runs Oct 9 to 16, 2026.

access.notes: Accessibility is not stated on the pages we read. The page suggests the small lot outside the animal adoption center, which is closest to the entrance.

first_step.how: Complete the online orientation and quiz on the Become a Volunteer page, then fill out the volunteer application. Approval can take up to a week.
first_step.basis: Clear public steps are posted and the site says how to apply, but volunteers need an online orientation, a quiz, and an approved application before the first shift.
first_step.what_to_expect: Shelter volunteers take an online orientation first, then are approved for a role such as cat socialization, dog walking, or photographing animals. Individual volunteers get specialized training before they handle animals, and shelter volunteers commit at least 3 hours a month. Groups and corporate teams do not handle dogs or cats, and corporate sessions run about 2 to 3 hours with a shelter tour.
first_visit_tips: Finish the online orientation and quiz before you come in
Park in the small lot outside the animal adoption center, closest to the entrance
Plan a visit between 10 am and 6 pm, when the lobby is open

records.notes: The homepage says the shelter is at critical capacity for cats and asks people not to bring cats in unless they are injured, sick, or in an emergency. Background check, parent consent for minors, and SEPTA directions are not stated on the pages we read. Group volunteers are also 18 or older unless the shelter agrees in advance.

records.name: Friends Pantry and Community Fridge
records.summary: A pantry and community fridge on the grounds of Arch Street Meeting House in Old City. Anyone in need can ask for help, and the pantry builds packages for each household.
records.what_you_do: Stop by the community fridge on weekdays, book a Sunday pantry pickup, or call to ask about volunteering or donating.

schedule.text: The community fridge is open on weekdays from 8 am until dusk, when the grounds are open. Pantry pickups are by appointment on Sundays, 1 to 2 pm.

cost.text: Free to use. Donations of food and household items are welcome.

access.notes: Wheelchair access, elevator, and entrance details are not stated on the pages we read. Fridge drop-offs depend on when the grounds are open.

first_step.how: Call or text (267) 334-0433 to book a Sunday pickup, or stop by the community fridge on a weekday.
first_step.basis: The pantry page says all are welcome to request help and gives a phone, text, and email to start. Its requirements line is unclear, so confirm what is needed when you call.
first_step.what_to_expect: A Sunday pantry pickup is a one hour appointment from 1 to 2 pm, booked by phone, text, or email. The fridge is open on weekdays from 8 am until dusk, and drop-offs depend on whether the meetinghouse grounds are open. Bulk food and household donations are arranged by calling or texting the same number.
first_visit_tips: Book your Sunday pickup ahead of time by phone, text, or email
Ask what to bring and whether you need proof of need, since the page does not say
Check museum hours before a weekday fridge visit, because drop-offs depend on when the grounds are open
Call (215) 413-1804 ext. 103 for museum hours

records.notes: The pantry requirements line on the site looks like a typo, so ask whether ID or proof of need is required. Six events are listed from Oct 17 to Dec 14, 2026. Volunteer roles, minimum age, and time commitment are not stated; the Get Involved section links to Contact Us and Opportunities pages instead.

records.name: Asociación Puertorriqueños en Marcha (APM)
records.summary: A Latino-based nonprofit in North Philadelphia that offers health and behavioral health care, foster care and adoption, family and children's services, early childhood education, and community and economic development.
records.what_you_do: Call the main office about the program you need, such as early childhood, foster care, or behavioral health. Volunteers can fill out an interest form for events such as the Sugar Cane Festival, the toy drive, or clean-up days.

schedule.text: The clinics at Rising Sun and Westmoreland are open Monday to Friday, 7 am to 5 pm, since June 22, 2026. Office hours are not posted. Early childhood programs run half day or full day, with no times listed.

cost.text: Head Start preschool is free for income-eligible families. Other program costs are not listed. Drug and alcohol treatment is listed as covered for people without insurance.

access.notes: The site describes its early childhood and mental health services as bilingual but does not name the languages. Accessibility is not stated on the pages we read.

first_step.how: Call 267-296-7200 or email info@apmphila.org and ask for the program you need. For early childhood, call 267-296-7357 or fill out the online enrollment form.
first_step.basis: There is a public phone line, office address, and interest form, but eligibility rules differ by program and are not all posted.
first_step.what_to_expect: These are services for clients, so a first step is a phone call or an online form rather than a walk-in visit. Eligibility depends on the program: income for Head Start and Pre-K Counts, or insurance for mental health and treatment. The volunteer form is an interest form, so expect a follow-up call rather than an immediate placement.
first_visit_tips: Have household income and insurance details ready when you call
Ask which languages staff speak before you visit
Expect a follow-up after you fill out the volunteer interest form

records.notes: This is a service provider rather than a drop-in group. The behavioral health team has its own email (BHteam@apmphila.org) and appointment line (267-296-7220). The volunteer page is an interest form and mentions COVID-19 limits. The tier 1 record showed a 2026 October date from a mapping data layer, not from APM's own page, so the last sign of life now uses the July 2026 board news.

records.name: Avalon String Band
records.summary: A Mummers string band with its address on South 2nd Street, the Two Street area. It welcomes beginners as well as experienced players and marches in the New Year's Day parade.
records.what_you_do: Play music, dance, or help as a marshal with the band in the New Year's Day parade. Non-players are welcome.

schedule.text: The band invites visitors to stop by on Tuesday nights, when it rehearses. The pages give no start time.

cost.text: Dues and costs are not published on the pages we read.

access.notes: Accessibility is not stated on the pages we read.

first_step.how: Stop by on a Tuesday night, or email avalonstringband1982@gmail.com for the join information PDF linked on the join page.
first_step.basis: The join page says the band welcomes beginners, invites visitors on Tuesday nights, and gives an email for more information. It does not describe what a visit involves.
first_step.what_to_expect: The join page does not describe a visit in detail. It invites musicians, dancers, and people who want to help as marshals to come by on a Tuesday night, when the band rehearses. Ask by email whether you should bring an instrument and what a first night looks like.
first_visit_tips: Email before you come to ask whether to bring an instrument
Ask for the join information PDF to read before your first visit
Dancers and marshals are welcome, not only players

records.notes: Contact addresses conflict across the site: the join page lists joinavalon@avalonstringband.com, the site's mailto link uses info@avalonstringband.com, and the Gmail address is shown as the main contact. Confirm which is current before listing it as the way in. The site's newest dated item is a July 2025 screenshot, so the 2026 January parade lineup is the newest evidence.

records.name: Bowerbird, INC.
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that presents music, dance and film, and runs synth classes and a free community synth studio.
records.what_you_do: Attend concerts and events, take synth classes, or book time at the free Community Synth Studio at AMLA and Esperanza. Support Bowerbird through its giving page.

schedule.text: The studio runs Oct 21 to Dec 17, 2026, Tuesday and Thursday 3 to 6 pm and Wednesday 3 to 9 pm, and is closed Thanksgiving week. Concerts run Oct 16 to 24, 2026. The Intro to Synths class is Oct 20, and Synth Foundations starts Oct 27.

locations.label: Community Synth Studio (AMLA Studios at Esperanza)
locations.transit: Free parking in the Esperanza lot on Bristol Street. Listed SEPTA routes are 47, 53, and 4.

cost.text: Studio time is free for all experience levels. Class and concert fees are not stated on the pages we read.

access.notes: Accessibility is not stated. The studio entrance is on Bristol Street through Esperanza's main doors.

requirements.gear: Studio users sign a user agreement, waiver, and code of conduct after signing up. Equipment is provided.

first_step.how: Attend a studio orientation or the Intro to Synths class on Oct 20, then email SoundLab@bowerbird.org to book studio time at least one week ahead.
first_step.basis: The studio says all experience levels are welcome and explains how to start: an orientation, an intro class, or the first 30 minutes of a first session.
first_step.what_to_expect: Studio time must be booked, in half-hour blocks up to two hours, and a studio manager is on site during open hours. After you sign up you receive an FAQ and sign a user agreement, waiver, and code of conduct. The studio has a range of synths, modular systems, a theremin, and small starter kits to try.
first_visit_tips: Email SoundLab@bowerbird.org at least a week ahead with a preferred time and a backup
Say whether you have done an orientation or an intro class
Park in the free Esperanza lot on Bristol Street, or take SEPTA routes 47, 53, or 4

records.notes: Correction: tier 1 marked the studio as drop-in, but the studio page says booking is required, by email one week ahead. The Intro to Synths flyer is an image with no readable time, place, or fee, so those details are not recorded. Studio inventory is listed as of Oct 8, 2026 and may change.

notes: Seven groups in batch w6-tier2-deep-a, each read from its own site with 2 to 4 fetches. Corrections to tier 1: Bowerbird's synth studio requires booking (not drop-in); Forbidden Fruit's festival took place Sept 12, 2026 and no later event is listed; ACCT Philly's shelter address is 111 W. Hunting Park Avenue and its main shelter takes volunteers 18 and older; Avalon String Band's contact addresses conflict across its pages. No searches were used, and no group was blocked. The budget was not exhausted.
